title: auth/header: unify scoped token semantics, add nonce/signing, and tighten CORS for OpenAI-compat
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: unify and clarify header semantics across Redwood's OpenAI-compatible API surface. Previously we had overlapping behaviors between project/org keys, scoped tokens, and our ad-hoc signing headers which caused ambiguity for tool-calling, streaming clients, and CORS policies. This PR introduces a single canonical mapping for incoming auth headers, formalizes scoped token resolution semantics (project vs org vs user-scoped), adds a nonce + signature header pair for replay-resistant request signing, and tightens CORS response headers for browser clients using OpenAI-compatible requests. The change preserves backward compatibility for common bearer flows but deprecates a few legacy headers with a migration window.
commits_summary: initial: auth: canonicalize header parsing and add scoped token resolver
feat: add X-Request-Nonce and X-Signature verification pipeline (HMAC-SHA256)
fix: ensure streaming endpoints respect CORS preflight for Authorization/Signature headers
docs: update openai-compat header docs and migration notes
tests: add unit/integration coverage for scoped tokens and signature verification
files_changed_summary: services/streaming/stream_handler.go: ensure CORS preflight handling for streaming SSE/WS upgrades
pkg/security/signature.go: new HMAC nonce/signature verifier and replay cache hooks
pkg/token/scoped_resolver.go: logic for project/org/user precedence and scope enforcement
docs/openai_compat/headers.md: updated semantics, examples, migration notes
tests/integration/auth_signing_test.go: new test harness for signed requests
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you clarify the precedence between project keys and org keys when both are present?

Author (Aisha Khan): Precedence is now explicit in the docs and enforced by scoped_resolver: token with explicit project scope > org-scoped token > account token. I added unit tests to cover the cases.
Greg Bennett: The nonce cache could be abused on the gateway. Have we bounded memory and ttl?
Author (Aisha Khan): Yes — replay cache is bucketed per-key with a 5 minute TTL and a soft limit per-bucket. Added comments and metrics to observe eviction rates.
Lina Morales: Streaming clients (browser) commonly hit CORS errors when adding custom headers. How will this change affect existing customers?

Author (Aisha Khan): We only widen Access-Control-Allow-Headers to include Authorization, X-Request-Nonce, X-Signature for endpoints that advertise openai-compat. For other endpoints default stricter CORS remains. Added migration note in docs and a feature flag to roll out stricter behavior gradually.
Ethan Park: Suggest making X-Request-Nonce name stable; consider X-Redwood-Request-Nonce to avoid collisions.
Author (Aisha Khan): Agreed on collision risk; kept the short header for OpenAI-compat but documented the alias X-Redwood-Request-Nonce and accept both for now. Plan to converge after one release.
Lina Morales: Approving after minor test adjustments.
release_notes: Unified header semantics for auth across OpenAI-compatible endpoints: scoped token precedence clarified (project > org > account), added nonce+signature headers for replay-resistant signing (X-Request-Nonce, X-Signature), tightened CORS and documented aliases. Backwards-compatible bearer flows preserved; deprecated X-Old-Auth header (see docs migration notes).
migration_notes: 1) Clients using legacy X-Old-Auth should switch to Authorization: Bearer <token> before the deprecation date. 2) If using browser-based streaming with custom headers, ensure preflight allows Authorization and X-Signature/X-Request-Nonce or use the documented SDK helpers that surface preflight-safe flows. 3) If relying on header aliases, prefer stable alias X-Redwood-Request-Nonce in next release.
compatibility_implications: OpenAI-compat: clients that set Organization: will continue to be supported; scoped tokens now have explicit resolution rules which may change which project is selected if multiple scopes are present. We accept both Authorization: Bearer (openai-style) and Redwood-specific X-Project-Key/X-Org-Key for a transition period.
security_notes: Signature verification uses HMAC-SHA256 with per-key secrets stored in the KMS-backed secrets store. Nonce replay window is 5 minutes, per-key bucketed cache with eviction metrics. Rate-limiter integration added to auth middleware to throttle repeated signature failures.
tests_summary: Added unit tests for scope resolution (project/org/user), signature verification including expired/invalid nonces, integration test covering streaming preflight with custom headers, and e2e test ensuring OpenAI-compatible Authorization header routes to same resolver.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag redwood.auth.header_unification controls rollout. Metric: auth.signature.failures, auth.replay.evictions, cors.preflight.failures. If we see increased cors.preflight.failures, rollback flag or add aliases in gateway config.
acknowledgements: Thanks to Security (Greg), API (Ethan), and Docs (Lina) for review and runtime validation. Special thanks to QA for the flaky-streaming-fix backports.
